summary: Separated metadata freshness and bounded stale-last-known-good behavior from artwork retention/eviction, and implemented bounded authoritative artifact retention/GC scheduled in production (addressing Phase 5 review MEDIUM finding #4). The user resolved reviewer finding 6.5-F1 by approving the half-window policy: the single configured MetadataStaleWindowMinutes (ADR-004, default 24h) is the TOTAL bounded last-known-good lifetime, split at half, so expiresAt = fetchedAt + window / 2 and staleUntil = fetchedAt + window. MetadataStateEntry now computes those boundaries, carries the explicit MetadataStateKind, and MetadataFreshness plus EvaluateFreshness/IsUsableAsCurrent/IsExpired evaluate the effective state: Fresh before the half boundary, bounded Stale (usable) from the half boundary up to the full boundary, and Expired and unusable as current at/after staleUntil, so new artwork publication must stop or retain the current usable artwork (the artwork pipeline that consumes this boundary is task 6.6). MetadataReconciliationProcessor publishes the window resolved from the current snapshot and, on a transient (ProviderUnavailable) read failure within the window, keeps the last-known-good snapshot as explicit Stale without extending the bounded timestamps; after the window the snapshot is neither kept nor refreshed as current. MetadataStateStore.ApplyRetention prunes only expired metadata records, and StateRetention.ApplyCacheRetention/StateRepository.ApplyRetention accept an exempt-kind set so metadata last-known-good state is never evicted by the render work-cache TTL/quota. ArtifactRetention is the bounded authoritative artifact GC: it protects the active image content hash, a live session's retained source artifact, and every artifact referenced by a non-terminal or recovery-blocked operation; retains a terminal-provenance source baseline only for the terminal retention window; reclaims superseded derived render output so the authoritative quota can be reused; applies a bounded just-promoted grace period; re-checks the authoritative reference records immediately before each delete (bounded constant-cost directory-generation comparison, reviewer finding 6.5-F3) so an artifact re-referenced after the reference snapshot is not removed; and fails closed when an authoritative state/operation record cannot be validated. SourceArtifactStore gained bounded artifact enumeration, a last-write-time lookup, and an explicit retention delete of the bytes and manifest. StateRetentionService is the hosted, bounded, cancellation-aware maintenance loop that schedules state retention, metadata freshness retention, and artifact GC in production. Reviewer finding 6.5-F2 (docs/changelog.md MetadataFreshnessTests case count) is corrected to the actual 10 cases. The task 6.1-6.4 queue, worker, metadata publication, recovery gate, and fence behavior is unchanged.

known_limitations: The freshness split is the user-approved policy (reviewer finding 6.5-F1 resolved): the configured MetadataStaleWindowMinutes is the total bounded last-known-good lifetime, expiresAt is the freshness half (fetchedAt + window / 2), and staleUntil is the end of the configured window (fetchedAt + window). A sub-tick degenerate window collapses the freshness half onto the full bound so the total stays positive and ordered; the validated configuration range is 5-10080 minutes, so this only affects direct callers of ComputeFreshnessWindow.

ArtifactRetention's F3 re-check compares the authoritative reference-record directory generation immediately before each delete and rebuilds the protected set when a record changed. This catches every reference made durable before the check and is bounded (constant cost in the common case), but it is not a distributed lock: a reference written in the residual interval between the check and the delete could still be missed. The just-promoted grace period and the next retention pass provide the outer safety margin, and the Jellyfin active image and restoration provenance (retained source) are unaffected by removing a derived render copy.

ArtifactRetention applies a fixed internal just-promoted grace period (default 1 hour) before an artifact can be reclaimed, closing the race in which a publication has promoted a new artifact but has not yet written the durable operation/state reference to it. This is a bounded safety margin, not a persisted user limit.

The metadata retention prune (MetadataStateStore.ApplyRetention) can race a concurrent metadata write between its read and delete; the worst case is deleting a just-written rebuildable cache entry, which is safe and simply refetched. Metadata is non-authoritative and no active/owned provenance is affected.

ArtifactRetention fails closed (returns 0) when any authoritative state/operation record cannot be validated, or when the number of records exceeds the bounded StateRepository.MaxEnumerationRecords (100000); a deployment above that bound would not run artifact GC rather than delete an unexamined reference.

The artwork pipeline that consumes IsUsableAsCurrent to stop or retain current artwork from expired metadata is task 6.6; 6.5 delivers and enforces the freshness boundary (including in the outage fallback) but does not create artwork work.
Only in-process validation was performed; no live Jellyfin host was available, consistent with the pinned-host absence noted for the environment. Host-guarded facts skip as expected.
